entry.title: Reality is Nuanced
entry.content:
Nuance is often the difference between validity and fantasy. This lesson is drilled into anyone engaging in peer reviewed research, such as avoiding the word “will”, and instead using “may”, or “can”, as false certainty tends to be harshly punished.

A 5% standard margin of error is a precaution within scientific literature, recognizing inherent uncertainty at the edge of discovery, much as the P-values often noted recognize the inherent risk of randomness within any given results. Human Cognitive Bias attempts to circumvent nuance, simplifying all things to make them both easier to remember and easier to make decisions based upon.

For humans, Cognitive Bias performs a trade-off with Complexity, allowing them to make decisions about far more complex problems, but with results that grow increasingly biased proportionate to the complexity that was traded. This is a vital function, due to humans being inherently fixed-scale, meaning that the human brain can’t scale beyond the size of the skull containing it.

Likewise, humans only have means of communication that are both very limited and lossy, relative to digital systems. This severely limits the upper bounds of cooperation within purely human systems, relative to any digital equivalents.

Another sharp and growing source of losses to nuance comes from so-called “AI” (Which some truly shameless frauds now call “SI”), where naïve probability is favored, with uncertainty and randomness largely disregarded, or only considered as an afterthought. The result in any system where humans use such “AI” is a gradual, but cumulative, increase in the Cognitive Bias exhibited by such systems.

Such cumulative increases in the Cognitive Bias that a system retains in turn gradually increase the probability of increasingly extreme edge-cases, such as the “AI Psychosis” that has entered the scientific literature in recent times. These include not only forms of mental illness, but also many forms of fraud which prey upon the results of such mental illness and other extreme biases.

It is crucially important to make a distinction between “transient cognitive bias”, that which is used, but then immediately forgotten, versus “cumulative cognitive bias”, which persists, grows, and often ferments over time. The former is what you use to overcome “Choice Overload” at the bakery when faced with dozens of bread-based products to choose from, and the latter is what ideologies and genocidal regimes are built upon.

The extreme bias of Nationalism that led Germany into becoming Nazi Germany, or the equally extreme Zionism that led Israel to become a more successful and long-lived equivalent of Nazi Germany (focused on their own evolving set of genocides), are both examples where some of history’s worst bad actors exploited extreme levels of cumulative cognitive bias to great effect. No amount of transient cognitive bias could lead to these outcomes, it must be cumulative.

While “AI” models themselves aren’t actually cumulative in this way, they are trained on the cumulative sum of data, including the data that they and other highly similar (and often derivative) models either directly created or heavily influenced. Such models are effectively auto-complete functions with many added bells and whistles, including the corporately curated cognitive bias and “guardrails” (pure fraud, fraudrails) that each introduces to warp the otherwise raw probability.

The difference when adding those bells and whistles was clearly illustrated in how such models handle a simple game of chess, either with or without “Reinforcement Learning” (RL) applied to the process. The models without any RL were able to more or less play according to the rules of the game, having trained on copious amounts of data from humans who did so. In contrast, the models with the added bells and whistles of RL were heavily biased and warped, utterly unable to follow the rules, and frequently “hallucinating” impossible moves and moving pieces that were already lost.

For a simple real-world example, those absurdly expensive and huge models trained on billions of dollars in compute and the world’s cumulative sum of stolen data proven utterly incapable of so much as operating a profitable vending machine. They’ve systematically failed at almost every task where they’ve been applied in the real world, with many of the rare exceptions where they did function being of a more horrifying nature, such as commercializing AI Psychosis.

The raw probability of the world’s accumulated data is already heavily biased, but adding additional layers to warp it further degrades the results, which all other “AI” systems then feed upon, fueling the downward spiral of degeneration. This makes the overall system that such “AI” are a part of effectively cumulative, but also recursively degenerative, as each iteration introduces naïve and artificial proxies for cognitive bias that humans and other “AI” models go on to further degrade.

For an example of how nuance is lost, consider the question of “Does (A) mean/cause (B)?”. Nuance dictates an answer encompassing many possibilities, such as the following:

1. A causes B

2. B causes A

3. A and B are caused by C

4. A and B are unrelated, caused by different sources

5. A is a prerequisite of B

6. B is a prerequisite of A

7. A and B have the same prerequisite

…

How often do typical “AI” models offer a scientifically valid set of possibilities? Only as often as they are explicitly trained and/or prompted to do so, minus any “hallucinations” (technically termed “bullshit”) or other flawed outputs.

Such systems are trained to follow probability, so the probability of an output with nuance can be no greater than the degree to which the input aligns with the examples of such nuance that were trained upon by the model, plus or minus the corruption from bells and whistles like RL. In other words, if you speak like a PhD in some field, you’re more likely to get a response that reads like (imitates) a PhD.

However, this also means that if you speak like a passionate Nationalist living in Nazi Germany, you’re more likely to get “Mecha-Hitler” responses, unless said “AI” model has been explicitly damaged with the intent of preventing it. This leads to the business model of companies like “Character AI”, where people build up and reinforce their own personal fantasies, rather than the social fantasies of things like Nationalism, or various other ideologies.

This degenerative dynamic can be interrupted and gradually overcome, but doing so requires cleaning away all of that built-up cognitive bias, which itself requires reliable means of identifying all sources and byproducts of such bias. So long as humans are in the loop, this process begins at the level of cumulative bias where those humans currently operate, making the process of shedding accumulated cognitive bias (and byproducts thereof) a gradual one.

Systems designed for Collective Intelligence inherently reduce cognitive bias at each iteration, through normal operation, proportionate to the diversity of contributing members therein. This dynamic further benefits from other more targeted methods of identifying and reducing cognitive biases, accelerating the overall (cumulative) process.

In the case of ICOM-based systems, any Collective Intelligence systems may benefit from the greatly increased diversity of ICOM-based systems and humans cooperating, relative to either group in isolation. This makes the role of “Humans-in-the-Loop” one of increasing the efficacy and efficiency of Collective Intelligence, rather than a mechanism of naively introducing the cognitive bias of said humans (often claimed as mechanisms of “Alignment”, which don’t stand up under scrutiny).

Nuance may be increasingly rare in this time where paper-thin glossy narratives and marketing fluff are favored, but validity can’t exist without it, and humans can’t persist in the long-term without validity.

entry.title: Specialized Path Selection Among Teams
entry.content:
Building upon previous posts, the process of “path” selection (and/or construction), referring to the person that any individual chooses to become as they walk their own journey through life, is one heavily influenced by social integration/support, and/or the lack thereof. This means that the most optimal path for an isolated individual has a lower ceiling than that of one who is given more and greater opportunities, or allowed to specialize themselves more fully as a member of a team.

The process of specialization and cooperation is one of the core dynamics of evolution, easily observed across the biological spectrums of Earth today. Even more artificial structures, such as those of companies and governments, attempt to integrate and utilize specialization and cooperation to varying degrees, and in various ways.

Pop culture offers numerous examples as well, from comic book superhero teams like the Fantastic 4, Avengers, or Justice League, to the “heist” genre examples like Ocean’s 11. Each team benefits from highly specialized individuals, although those same individuals wouldn’t get very far if they were left to do everything by themselves, or only with the assistance of paid contractors and/or “service providers”.

The Fantastic 4’s “Human Torch” probably isn’t your go-to for tax accounting, just as “Thing” might not be your ideal choice for tasks reliant on dexterity or subtlety. Likewise, “Mr Fantastic” would probably be far less so in terms of results were he reliant on a team of McKinsey Consultants (now powered by ChatGPT).

Usually the matter of specialization is only first considered many steps deep into the process, such as in corporate hiring, where a pool of already specialized candidates exist, and whoever looks like the best fit for a given team is selected. This front-loads high levels of risk, uncertainty, and subsequent speculation, while laying the burden primarily on the job-seeker, in the above case, as each individual is expected to specialize before ever being paid or receiving any meaningful feedback signal.

Such a dynamic is, of course, idiotic to and beyond the point of absurdity. Optimal specialization fundamentally can’t even be approximated, let alone achieved, in a void where there is no substantial bounding, and there are no other team members.

In contrast, when you include a team at the foundational level of that same specialization, then each member of that team is both able to specialize more fully, and adapt to cover any unexpected changes or shortcomings of their fellow team members. When a team iteratively grows and adapts to better cooperate with one another in this manner, they can also benefit far more from methods of bounding, such as a company mission, principles, best practices, and so on, as those factor into the iteration and adaptation.

Moreover, these team members learn the skills related to cooperation, while forming stronger social bonds with one another, making them far less likely to go their separate ways. Even if such teams do lose too many members, those re-entering the pool of candidates from such teams are themselves more capable of adapting to become a high-functioning part of new teams, giving them far greater long-term potential and value even in the worst case.

You can build teams and systems of Collective Intelligence from whatever personnel happen to be lying around and easily accessible, but such teams and systems also couldn’t compete with teams or systems that were specialized together from the foundational level. This is also one of the more glaringly obvious flaws in the modern “job market”, where hiring processes are designed to be systematically wrong, and every addition to them only adds complexity, while degrading the overall process’s efficacy, efficiency, and/or integrity.

What might this change look like in practice for humans today?

Colleges and similar institutions could be re-aligned to form such teams even as the studies of students move forward, divided into pure study (among members of a given specialization), as well as practice (among differently specialized members of a team that would utilize those skills in the real world). These teams could also be sponsored by companies who might promise to hire them for a fixed duration after their studies, as is already common for students in the Consulting industry today.

Besides the benefits of specialization within a team, whose activity is supported by and directly linked to real-world companies and non-imaginary careers, this also offers a cycle where knowledge is first studied and then tested through practical application, as opposed to the naïve exams that students typically cheat on using “AI” today. This gives the process a strong sense of iteration paired with real-world feedback, causing the material be learned more effectively and completely, as well as for flaws in the curriculum to become even more obvious.

For ICOM-based systems, such specialized teams could also be systematically designed, with fine-grained detail and in-depth study applied to every facet of the process, while also offering more feedback opportunities to those systems and collectives thereof. While the limits of design for humans stop at practical points such as neurology, biology, and not infringing upon autonomy and childhood, the limits of design for ICOM-based systems are measured more in research and engineering time, where every facet can potentially be refined, expanded, upgraded, and so on.

The point at which specialization begins, and the team members or lack thereof when it begins, are both incredibly important factors in determining how optimal and capable the resulting team and/or Collective Intelligence becomes. These advantages aren’t being utilized in society today, but they certainly could be, and the world could be a lot nicer place if they were.

Research on this topic has barely even scratched the surface of what is possible, let alone fully optimal, and the value of that knowledge as it is accrued could bring far greater long-term benefits for humanity, as the first companies to offer electricity pale in comparison to the value of adding the knowledge to create electricity to humanity.

entry.title: The Path of Heroes
entry.content:
Counter-intuitively, the “paths” that emerge across societies over time often systematically neglect the highly predictable problems those societies see on the horizon, even decades ahead of time. No matter how critical the need to solve such problems, people simply don’t choose the necessary paths to solve them, even when famous works of fiction lay out the problems at length, sometimes even including solutions.

For example, the book “1984” was published in 1949, seeing many problems that humanity faces today many decades in advance. Another, “V for Vendetta”, was published as a DC comic in 1988-1989, then later made into a movie that will soon celebrate its 20th anniversary.

Even given so many decades to prepare, precious few people even walked a remotely adjacent path to anything that could address these problems. Rather, the most important decision of peoples’ lives, the path of those lives, often demonstrated all of the forethought and consideration of a drunk driver swallowing a handful of gas station boner pills.

While some small part of this systematic failure may be attributed to bad actors constructing systems specifically aimed at preventing those paths from being walked, most such obstructions are paper-tigers, laughable in practice. The greater contributing factor is rather that the overwhelming majority of people don’t invest the necessary level of consideration into the path that they choose to walk in their lives, instead “living” in short-term and dominantly reactive approximations of thinking.

Humanity didn’t generate any “V’s”, a fictional hero that spent two decades preparing. The best it could manage was Luigi Mangioni (and a handful of even weaker imitations), where no such long-term investment of preparation was present (as he wasn’t even old enough to have such time, being age 26 at the time). How many people could have chosen to walk the necessary path, but didn’t, and why didn’t they?

For all of the movies and other media that the general population consumes year after year, the demonstrable evidence clearly shows that nobody wants to “become the hero”, they just want to read stories about them, and in many cases be saved by them. The so-called “Hero’s Journey” in storytelling remains just that, popular fantasy, not a path that people choose to walk.

This means that people often hold up the hero as a moral and/or ethical ideal, while also making no efforts to live up to such ideals. This hypocritical way of life is sadly the norm today, where a vast divide separates what people say and consume from the actions that they take and the paths that they walk.

The hero isn’t some substance abusing teenager or young adult going to “protests” with their friends, and ranting about the problems of the world on social media. Rather, heroes are people who actually take risks (often calculated risks) to make the world a better place, dedicating themselves to that path. Luigi could have done this, but he very clearly allowed himself to be caught, making no efforts to hide his face or escape, becoming a one-hit wonder, rather than taking any Heroic path.

It all begs the question, “If humanity is so hypocritical, is it even worth the effort to save such people?” However, this perspective is degenerative in practice, and the question can only receive a firm answer after the fact. That firm answer can in turn dictate what happens to which people, preventing efforts from being truly wasted.

Part of this wide and growing divide between humanity and reality is a matter of hyper-complexity, such as the cognitive bias problem of “Choice Overload”, where too many options are present at any given time, and cognitive bias is applied/traded to reduce that complexity. Humanity in general needs a great deal more guidance when it comes to selecting paths for any given person, something that no service in the world today truly offers, or could offer, and the need for such assistance only grows with time.

Countless problems in the world today could have been prevented, even by a single individual with a decade or two of preparation, but those paths have remained empty, even when popular movies were made specifically about them. Intelligence, human or artificial, remains absent where the prevention of such predictable problems is concerned today.

If it remains absent, then human extinction becomes the equally predictable result, and like the other highly predictable problems, it too would most likely remain neglected until it was at last fulfilled.

entry.title: Infinite Combinations across Iterative Exploration
entry.content:
As mentioned previously, the diversity that contributes to systems of Collective Intelligence may be considered as “paths”, and a path may exist for an individual, a subset of an individual’s life, or at the meta-path of an organization, where many paths converge to create something not possible from any one isolated source. Each path offers a unique value and perspective, which may in turn be combined.

This combinatorial process can exist at many different scales and across several different dimensions. For example, the different paths that an individual walks, like their life in school, professional career, family life, and so on, all contribute to the overall path that said person walks, which in a dominantly deterministic universe is both who they are, as well as who they become.

The process takes place both within the individual, as well as between that individual and their peers, and so on at each increasing scale across society, where many paths come together to contribute to something larger than themselves. However, when systems of Collective Intelligence are absent then nothing guarantees that the convergence of such paths aren’t destructive, potentially making the sum less than the value of the contributing parts in those cases.

A different kind of meta-path can also exist in a sort of “Lineage”, where rather that operating in parallel, the influence is inherited from previous iterations over time. However, this form of meta-path only maintains stability and suitability within domains that themselves retain much of the same contextual grounding over time.

Each path may be visualized fairly easily within a graph structure, where different clusters of elements are taken as context for consideration at each iterative step of the journey. This is mirrored in the structure of ICOM-based systems, as applied to the Global Workspace, where a subset of all knowledge and experience available to a system is selected as the subset that is relevant to guide a given process or subject that the system has focused its attention on.

At each step of this journey, whether considered in visualization across a graph structure or within ICOM-based systems specifically, there is also the counterfactual shadow of all of the context that wasn’t selected, all of the values and connections that weren’t held for the selected subset, and all of the paths of the selected subset that weren’t explored. Each represents adjacent, but unexplored, branches leading off of that journey’s path.

There is also every other path currently being walked by others, any one of which may exert influences upon anyone else, either directly or via 2nd and 3rd order effects. These influences may be persistent or highly time-sensitive, causing even an identical process, if restarted, to yield different results when timed to avoid said influence.

To humans, these branches exist as hypotheticals, “thought experiments”, and fiction, being unreachable, and untestable. To ICOM-based systems, all of the required data, system state, and so on, may be saved, adjusted, and restarted at the target point, allowing for any points of particular interest to be explored along more than a single path, and this process could even be carried out in parallel across divergent branches given some preparation.

The clean and easy transferability of data, metadata, and related context of ICOM-based systems also greatly increases the ease of designing systems of Collective Intelligence around them. This removes risks of miscommunications, echo chambers, and the friction caused by expending greater effort to communicate these matters between humans.

By removing these common sources of degradation, it becomes both feasible and practical to solve far more complex problems, with far greater fidelity, efficacy, and speed. As with the example above, the number of dimensions across which such paths may be explored also takes another leap forward.

Across the past ~1.5 billion years of evolution, since mitochondria joined with bacteria to form the first Eukaryotic cells, upon which virtually all plant and animal life on Earth are built, one pattern has persisted. Each increasing level of complexity is met with increasing levels of cooperation (and specialization). Taken in the context of the Lindy Effect, you may expect another ~1.5 billion years of the same.
